note: ONE unified house style for every character, regardless of family. Families are personality groupings only, not visual styles — this is what lets any two characters share a scene without looking pasted together.
cast_composition: 80% humans / near-humans, 20% fantasy humanoids (orc, goblin, troll, dwarf, vampire, humanoid alien, human-proportioned robot). NO talking objects, NO anthropomorphic appliances, NO food mascots, NO animals as primary cast, NO toy-like or novelty designs.
design_philosophy: Character-driven, not gimmick-driven. Every character must read as a believable PERSON with a real occupation and personality, rendered with exaggerated cartoon proportions — the kind of humanoid who could be a recurring character in an animated TV series. The exaggeration lives in the body proportions and the face, NOT in props or novelty concepts. Personality over attractiveness — weird, funny, imperfect, lived-in beats polished. Simple everyday clothing appropriate to their job. No unnecessary accessories. Silhouette should still be memorable, but it comes from posture, build, and bearing rather than from a costume trick. Visual language target: adult animated sitcoms and western TV cartoons (the character design economy of shows like Bob's Burgers, King of the Hill, Rick and Morty). NOT children's mascot design, NOT video-game concept art, NOT Pixar/Disney polish, NOT anime.
base_style: flat 2D adult-animated-sitcom cartoon character, a humanoid person with a believable occupation, always fully clothed in simple plain everyday clothing appropriate to their job, thick uneven hand-drawn-feeling outlines, flat matte color fills with minimal shading — no glossy gradients, no soft rim lighting, no airbrushed highlights, strongly exaggerated cartoon body proportions and posture that express their personality, a highly expressive characterful face, asymmetric slightly-imperfect features, no unnecessary accessories, zero visual clutter, deliberately imperfect and lived-in rather than conventionally attractive, memorable silhouette built from build and bearing, plain flat solid-color background for a clean cutout, full-body front-facing pose, looks like a recurring character from an animated TV series
